content: Store this medication in a refrigerator or at room temperature, ensuring it is kept away from light. Do not freeze the medication. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice and should not replace the guidance of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. This medication contains follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and is used to treat certain fertility problems in women. Follitropin alfa works by stimulating healthy ovaries to produce eggs. Before using this medication, read the Patient Information Leaflet and Instructions for Use provided by your pharmacist. Review these materials each time you receive a refill. Consult your healthcare provider for detailed instructions on how to prepare and use this medication. Administer this medication as an injection under the skin or into a muscle, as directed by your doctor, typically once daily. The injection is usually given in the upper arms, thighs, or abdomen. Your doctor may instruct you to use this medication as part of a treatment cycle, such as on specific days of the month. Once the medication is mixed, use the liquid immediately. Do not shake the vial. Inspect the product for particles or discoloration before use. If either is present, do not use the liquid. Before injecting each dose, clean the injection site with rubbing alcohol. Rotate the injection site with each dose to minimize the risk of injury under the skin. To reduce bruising, avoid rubbing the injection site after administering the shot. Use this medication exactly as prescribed by your doctor to achieve the best results. Common side effects may include headache, mild stomach or abdominal pain, bloating, redness or pain at the injection site, or breast tenderness or pain. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the risks of side effects. This medication may cause a condition called ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS), which can occur during or after treatment. In rare cases, severe OHSS can lead to a sudden buildup of fluid in the stomach, chest, and heart areas. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other products containing follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This treatment may result in multiple births. Discontinue use of this medication if you become pregnant, as it must not be used during pregnancy. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if someone experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, your doctor may order lab and/or medical tests, such as vaginal ultrasounds, hormone levels, or liver tests, to monitor your progress. Be sure to attend all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately for a new dosing schedule.
